newsitem.title: USA: USDA cheese price to help set milk marketing order.
newsitem.headline: USDA cheese price to help set milk marketing order.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday it would use its new weekly cheese price, which debuts Friday, to calculate the basic formula price for milk.
It would replace the cheese price from National Cheese Exchange in the formula. The exchange closed April 25.

USDA's cheese price will be based on a survey of U.S. cheddar cheese manufacturers who sell cheese on a bulk, wholesale basis. The survey will provide weighted average prices for 40 lb blocks, 640 lb blocks and 500 lb barrels.
The survey covers 80 to 85 percent of all bulk cheddar cheese sales.

"The new cheese price series being factored into the basic formula price will significantly contribute to improved market information for the dairy industry," said Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, "while allowing the current longer-term proces of reforming federal milk marketing orders, including possible replacement of the (basic formula price), to continue without disruption."
The basic formula price serves as the basis for establishing minimum prices for fluid milk under the marketing order system.
There had been complaints the National Cheese Exchange price was not representative.
